papers.title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks
papers.summary: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn mechanical systems from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving the dynamics through the Euler-Lagrange equations, biasing the model toward motion that respects the variational structure of mechanics. The interactions studied so far have been pairwise-additive, leaving open whether LNNs can recover an irreducible many-body interaction from motion alone. We address this using the Axilrod-Teller triple-dipole interaction, the leading three-body dispersion term, whose dependence on the collective geometry of three particles cannot be represented by any sum of pairwise terms. We prescribe the kinetic energy exactly and learn only the potential, as a function of interparticle distances and angles. Combined with a signal-aware sampling strategy that concentrates training data where the three-body signal is strongest while preserving broad coverage of configuration space, this recovers the interaction from accelerations alone. The learned potential reproduces the radial scaling, angular dependence, and characteristic sign reversal of the Axilrod-Teller interaction, and generates stable trajectories. Embedding it within a pairwise Lennard-Jones potential lets us examine its observability: the three-body term is recovered once its dynamical signature exceeds the residual modeling error, which it does cleanly at amplified coupling but not at the coupling of a real noble gas, bracketing the transition between the two. Finally, symbolic regression on the trained potential, with no assumed functional form, returns the Axilrod-Teller expression with angular numerator, radial law, and coupling constant intact. An LNN with domain-specific structure can thus recover an irreducible three-body interaction from trajectories as a closed-form law, pointing toward learning interaction laws whose structure is not known a priori.

papers.title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
papers.summary: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

papers.title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
papers.summary: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.

papers.title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver
papers.summary: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
papers.summary: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

papers.title: Spatial Context or Memory? Sizing the Inputs of Neural Surrogates for Partially Observed Fields
papers.summary: Neural surrogates that forecast a physical field from sparse, noisy sensors read a window of nearby sensors and a history of past snapshots. Practitioners choose both by comparing fitted models with each other. Such comparisons cannot tell a model's shortfall from missing information. We measure the trade-off between window and history against the Bayes-optimal error of the same readings. An exact Gaussian analysis shows that noisy or sparse observation of a field with local dynamics makes the optimal forecast read distant sensors only through spatial correlation. On a forced linear field with a known optimum, trained models that read only the window come within 1% of it. We then train such models on viscous Burgers flow and the chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky (KS) equation, with every deciding comparison fixed before any test evaluation. In every field except KS, eight snapshots remove a smaller fraction of the one-snapshot error as the lead time, the number of steps to the forecast target, grows. In KS, for windows up to one correlation length, they remove a larger fraction. This lead-time inversion persists across sensor densities, three architectures and a two-dimensional domain. It shrinks as damping lowers the Lyapunov exponent. Damping also removes the linear instability of KS. We therefore tie the inversion to instability and leave chaos and linear amplification unseparated. For surrogate design the results give two rules. Size the window in correlation lengths of the field. Split a fixed input budget between window and history for the lead time the model will serve, because the best split moves toward wider windows as the lead time grows. In Burgers flow the split chosen at lead time one ends with 13.5 times the best error at lead time eight.
papers.title_ja: 空間的コンテキストか記憶か？部分的に観測された場のニューラルサロゲートの入力サイズ設定

papers.title: Polyconvex neural-network surrogates with learned paired directional features for anisotropic hyperelastic homogenization
papers.summary: Approximating the effective anisotropic hyperelastic response of a representative volume element (RVE) requires constitutive expressiveness, mechanical consistency, and computational efficiency. This work develops a polyconvex physics-augmented neural network (PANN) construction based on paired directional features whose orientations, stretch powers, and determinant exponents adapt to the RVE response. The features are composed with convex, componentwise nondecreasing cores, realized as an input-convex neural network (ICNN) or an input-convex Kolmogorov-Arnold network (ICKAN). The complete energies satisfy objectivity, an exactly stress-free reference, two-dimensional polyconvexity, and prescribed growth conditions by construction, and nonnegative energy is certified separately for the selected models. On a multicavity and a single-cavity periodic cell, these energies are compared with an Unconstrained energy, trained identically without the curvature and growth constraints, and with three hyperreduced projection-based reduced-order models (HPROMs), which serve as physics-based references. On the first cell, learning the features lowers the stress error sevenfold, and six features suffice on both. The constrained energies remain below one percent in stress error and in the displacement error of a tensile-coupon FE$^2$ application with a full-order reference, whereas the Unconstrained energy and the HPROMs are more accurate inside the data. Beyond the data, however, the Unconstrained energy loses rank-one convexity, and under confined compression it stops below half of the 500 MPa that the constrained energies reach. These results quantify what the guarantees cost in accuracy and what they secure beyond the data.

papers.title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
papers.summary: Neural operators that learn physical laws from data should generalize beyond their training distribution and expose the learned law in closed form. The Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator achieves both for position-dependent dynamics by learning a dense pseudo-differential symbol over all positions and frequencies, at a cost that grows with the square of the resolution and with closed forms that must be read out by hand. This dense symbol is unnecessary: a finite-order variable-coefficient differential operator has a symbol whose separation rank is bounded by the number of its coefficient functions, independently of the resolution, and the symbols that this network learns on its own benchmarks have rank two. We introduce the Kolmogorov-Arnold flow (KAFlow), which learns the generator of a physical operator as a low-rank symbol built from univariate Kolmogorov-Arnold functions, fixes the gauge of these functions so that every term has a unique place, integrates the dynamics with exact exponential integrators, and distills its closed form automatically. On the synthetic benchmarks of the Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator, KAFlow lowers the out-of-distribution loss by 3.4 to 11 times and recovers every coefficient to within 10^-4 without symbolic templates, reaching the precision floor of the data. On long-horizon quantum dynamics, it lowers the state infidelity by up to 6 orders of magnitude, and by 30 times when trained only on position and momentum measurements. KAFlow also learns a variable-order fractional operator 15 times more accurately than existing operator networks and discovers nonlocal, fractional and non-polynomial dispersion relations on which sparse regression fails.

papers.title: SBNO : Schr\"odinger Bridge Neural Operator for the Forward and Inverse Problems under Missing Information
papers.summary: Partial differential equation (PDE) surrogate modeling often relies on either dense observations or access to governing equations/physics constraints. In practice, observations can be sparse and partial, and the underlying physics may be partially specified or unavailable. We introduce SBNO, an equation-free paired-data diffusion bridge matching framework that learns conditional operators for both forward and inverse PDE problems under partial observations. SBNO uses diffusion Schr\"odinger bridge matching to learn a pair of time-dependent drifts from a mask-aware endpoint coupling that preserves empirical input-solution pairing during training and supports both PDE-task directions within a single framework. At inference time, SBNO produces a deterministic point reconstruction by integrating the probability-flow ODE constructed from the learned drift pair, without inference-time observation or PDE guidance-weight tuning. On five PDE benchmarks with 5% observations, SBNO achieves superior or comparable accuracy to baselines while demonstrating lower test-instance error dispersion. Furthermore, SBNO is at least $9.7 \times$ faster and reduces GPU memory by at least $4.3 \times$ compared to guided-diffusion baselines.
papers.title_ja: SBNO: 欠損情報下における前向き・逆問題のためのシュレーディンガーブリッジニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、観測データが疎である場合や物理法則が不明確な場合でも、偏微分方程式（PDE）の前向きおよび逆問題を解くための「SBNO」を提案する。拡散モデルのシュレーディンガーブリッジマッチングを用い、マスク認識型のエンドポイント結合により、学習時に入力と解の対応を維持しながら条件付きオペレータを学習する。推論時には確率流ODEを積分することで決定論的な再構成を行い、観測やPDEのガイダンス重みの調整を不要とする。5%の観測率という厳しい条件下で、既存手法と同等以上の精度を維持しつつ、テストインスタンスのエラー分散を低減し、計算速度は9.7倍以上、GPUメモリ使用量は4.3倍以上の効率化を実現した。

papers.title: Physical-state supervision for design-only Gaussian process surrogates of implosion simulations
papers.summary: Physical diagnostics recorded during simulation can organize a sharply varying response, but using them as surrogate inputs normally requires another calculation at prediction. We construct a physical-state-supervised Gaussian process surrogate that learns these diagnostics from design variables. Cross-fitted state estimates augment a retained design representation; a global Gaussian process and an optional soft mixture of response-band experts use identical inputs. On a database of 1,987 paired one-dimensional implosions, learned burn-weighted states from calculations without alpha-particle heating reduce mean squared log-response error by 60.25% and 52.98% for the global predictor on random holdout and design-space extrapolation. Random-projection and shuffled-state supervision do not reproduce these gains. For CH, matched-input comparisons show that experts help at smaller training budgets but contribute little at 1,000 designs with this representation. A thermal-feedback benchmark validates the complete learned-state procedure, while 3,000 newly calculated Be/Cocktail designs expose weaker extrapolation gains and cases where experts degrade accuracy. A conditional state-error bound separates encoding sensitivity from routing effects. An open Python implementation reproduces the archived predictions and is released with the data, per-design results, and measured costs. Physical-state supervision is thus a useful representation for finite-data surrogates, whereas expert specialization should be selected by validation.

papers.title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
papers.summary: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$\alpha$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$\alpha$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.
papers.title_ja: 高速フーリエ：ニューラルオペレータによる原惑星円盤の放射モデリング高速化

papers.title: Non intrusive parametric Reduced Order Models based on physics for incompressible flow
papers.summary: Reduced order modeling provides an efficient alternative to high fidelity simulations for the rapid prediction of fluid flows in many query settings. Among non intrusive approaches, Operator Inference (OpInf) enables the identification of reduced dynamical operators directly from data while preserving a prescribed mathematical structure. The present work extends physics structured OpInf to the construction of parametric Reduced Order Models for transient incompressible flows governed by the Navier-Stokes equations. The velocity and pressure fields are represented using separate global reduced bases, and their reduced operators are identified directly from temporal and parametric POD coefficients. The identification procedure is formulated as a sequence of uncoupled least squares problems, leading to an efficient offline stage while avoiding the explicit projection of the governing equations. The approach is first evaluated on a lid driven cavity flow in a periodic regime to assess temporal extrapolation and prediction at previously unseen parameter values. Its applicability is then demonstrated for transient flow through a porous medium with a square obstacle, for which the nonlinear terms are not directly amenable to a standard Galerkin projection. The results demonstrate that the approach can accurately reproduce both velocity and pressure fields while providing computationally efficient predictions for unseen parameter values.
papers.title_ja: 非侵入型物理ベースパラメトリック縮約モデルによる非圧縮流の解析
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ナビエ・ストークス方程式で記述される非圧縮流に対して、物理構造を保持する非侵入型縮約モデル（OpInf）を構築する手法を提案する。速度場と圧力場をそれぞれ独立した縮約基底で表現し、時間・パラメータPOD係数から直接縮約演算子を同定することで、支配方程式の明示的な射影を回避する。離散化された最小二乗問題として定式化されることでオフライン計算を効率化し、既知のパラメータ値での予測精度と、未見パラメータ値への外挿能力をlid driven cavity流や多孔質媒体流で検証した。結果として、非線形項が標準的なガレルキン射影に適用しにくいケースでも、計算効率を維持しつつ速度・圧力場を高精度に再現できることを示した。

papers.title: Algebraic Integer Quantization for Machine Learning Applications
papers.summary: In this article, we propose algebraic integer number formats (AINF) as a framework for highly configurable and accurate compressed computation. A key property of AINF is its straightforward reduction to purely integer arithmetic, enabling error-free multiply-accumulate operations. We develop a matrix multiplication engine that exploits this property, obtaining performance within a predictable factor of the most efficient numerical counterparts on modern hardware accelerators. Another key advantage of AIQ is the freedom to select algebraic integers tailored to the numerical characteristics of a given use case, offering optimization opportunities that are fundamentally unavailable in floating-point or fixed-point formats. Motivated by these properties, we introduce algebraic integer quantization (AIQ), a lossy compression format for large language model (LLM) inference, and provide results demonstrating that AIQ achieves competitive accuracy compared to the industry-standard MX format across a diverse set of models and benchmarks at equivalent bit-per-parameter budgets. The experiments presented in this article employ algebraic integers of degree two (quadratic integers); generalizations to higher-order and, in particular, multidimensional algebraic integers promise even greater computational advantages and remain a promising direction for future work.
papers.title_ja: 機械学習アプリケーションのための代数整数量子化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、高精度な圧縮計算を可能にする代数整数数値形式（AINF）を提案する。この形式は整数演算に還元可能であり、誤差のない乗算加算操作を実現できる。さらに、大規模言語モデル（LLM）推論向けの損失圧縮形式「代数整数量子化（AIQ）」を導入し、業界標準のMX形式と比較して同等のビット予算で競争力のある精度を維持することを示した。

papers.title: Sample-Adaptive Zeroth-Order Post-Training
papers.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization offers a memory-efficient alternative to backpropagation for fine-tuning large language models. However, existing ZO methods typically sample training examples uniformly, overlooking their evolving importance and leaving avoidable estimation variance. To address this limitation, we propose Sample-Adaptive Zeroth-Order Optimization (SAZO), which learns sample importance online and adaptively allocates queries to accelerate convergence. SAZO extracts gradient-norm information from existing directional differences to estimate sample importance without access to true gradients. Furthermore, to track evolving importance from sparse minibatch feedback, SAZO maintains per-example exponential moving averages that aggregate observations across updates. The method requires no additional model evaluations and only $O(N)$ additional scalar state compared with MeZO. We prove that SAZO asymptotically matches the leading convergence term of the minimum-variance sampling oracle, and achieves a strictly faster convergence rate than standard methods. Extensive experiments across four model families demonstrate improved average downstream performance and up to $6\times$ faster convergence to the same training loss in terms of query count.
papers.title_ja: サンプル適応型ゼロ次ポストトレーニング
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデルのファインチューニングにおいて、バックプロパゲーションを不要とするゼロ次最適化手法の効率化を提案する。既存手法が訓練データを均等にサンプリングする問題に対し、サンプルの重要度をオンラインで学習し、クエリを適応的に割り当てるSAZO手法を設計した。真の勾配にアクセスせずに勾配ノルム情報を推定し、指数移動平均により重要度の変化を追跡することで、追加のモデル評価なしで収束を加速する。4つのモデルファミリーでの実験により、同等の損失達成までのクエリ数が最大6倍高速化し、下流タスクの性能向上も示された。

papers.title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules
papers.summary: Sparse computation can scale the parametric capacity of LLMs without proportionally increasing active computation, but pretraining sparse architectures remains expensive and data-hungry. Existing sparse upcycling methods mainly target Mixture-of-Experts models, where expert homogeneity, sample inefficiency, and system overheads can limit practical scalability. Static sparse memory offers predictable access and token-specific updates that can help address these challenges, but naively integrating it into pretrained computation yields poor returns. In this work, we introduce STAPLE, a recipe built upon STEM for integrating static sparse memory into pretrained models. Whereas STEM replaces FFN up-projections with token-indexed embeddings, STAPLE retains them and adds the embeddings as a residual pathway, preserving pretrained computation while learning complementary token-specific information in a scalable manner. On OLMo-2 1B, STAPLE improves over continued dense training by 4.27 points on HumanEval, 2.80 on MBPP, 2.27 on GSM8K, and 1.65 on DROP. Average performance increases with static capacity, and improvements persist on the larger OLMo-2 7B backbone. STAPLE also outperforms static sparse baselines such as STEM and an Engram-style model, and achieves a higher average score than an MoE upcycling baseline while decoding 2x faster with less than half its GPU model memory and measured GPU energy per token in our throughput-oriented decoding evaluation. Importantly, despite introducing billions of parameters late in training, our host-offloaded implementation keeps generation throughput within 1.5% and training throughput within 3% of the dense baseline, while caching only the ~5% most frequent embeddings on GPU. These results show that static sparse memory can provide a sample-efficient, scalable, and sustainable path for expanding pretrained models without sparse pretraining from scratch.
papers.title_ja: STAPLE: 埋め込みモジュールを用いた事前学習済みチェックポイントの静的スパースアップサイクリング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、事前学習済みLLMに静的スパースメモリを効率的に統合する手法STAPLEを提案する。既存のMoEベース手法とは異なり、FFNのアッププロジェクションを保持しつつ、トークン固有の情報を残差経路として追加することで、事前学習の計算を維持しつつ補完的な知識を獲得する。OLMo-2モデルでの実験により、継続的な密な学習やMoEアップサイクリングと比較して、HumanEvalやGSM8Kなどのベンチマークで性能向上を示した。さらに、GPUメモリ使用量とエネルギー効率を大幅に改善しながら、推論速度を2倍に高速化し、スループットへの影響を最小限に抑えることを実証している。

papers.title: TreeHCA: Hindsight-Guided Exploration and Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents
papers.summary: Outcome-supervised group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) assigns the same advantage to every token in an LLM agent trajectory, leaving useful and unhelpful decisions undifferentiated. Hindsight credit assignment (HCA) can refine this feedback, but its estimates rely on trajectories containing informative alternatives at consequential histories. We introduce TreeHCA, which couples hindsight-guided exploration with hindsight credit assignment. TreeHCA uses changes in reference-answer likelihood to revisit intermediate histories and sample alternative continuations, forming a tree of reasoning and tool interactions. Because this exploration changes the distribution of sampled continuations, we derive the corresponding inverse-hindsight importance correction, including an exact finite-pool identity. We use this structure in a normalized tree backup that propagates terminal outcomes into turn-level advantages. This shared hindsight structure is TreeHCA's central design principle, linking informative exploration with hindsight-guided credit assignment. Across seven question-answering benchmarks and three Qwen backbones, TreeHCA outperforms all baselines in aggregate exact match, validating the effectiveness of paired exploration and credit assignment for multi-turn LLM agent training. Our code is available at github.com/TheBlackCat22/TreeHCA.
papers.title_ja: TreeHCA: マルチターンLLMエージェントのための後見ガイド探索とクレジット割り当て
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、マルチターンLLMエージェントの学習において、トークン単位の利得を均一に扱う従来の手法の限界を克服するTreeHCAを提案する。後見クレジット割り当て（HCA）と、参照回答の尤度変化に基づく中間履歴の再訪・代替継続のサンプリングを組み合わせ、推論ツリーを構築する。この探索による分布変化に対応する逆後見重要性補正を導出し、ターンの利得に伝播させる正規化ツリーバックアップを実装した。7つのQAベンチマークで既存手法を上回る性能を示し、探索とクレジット割り当ての統合がエージェント訓練に有効であることを実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と強化学習手法の融合であり、ユーザーの関心と高度に一致する。

papers.title: Kronecker Product Attention: Memory-Efficient KV Compression via Structured Factorization
papers.summary: Efficient autoregressive generation is increasingly limited by the memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length, batch size, and model depth. Existing approaches such as Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), and Tensor Product Attention (TPA) reduce this cost through different trade-offs, but often sacrifice expressivity, require additional positional-encoding machinery, or impose restrictive low-rank structure. We propose Kronecker Product Attention (KPA), which represents key and value activations as sums of Kronecker products of compact, token-dependent matrix factors. KPA strictly generalizes TPA: rank-one vector-outer-product factorization arises as a degenerate Kronecker split, while non-degenerate matrix factors can represent richer block-structured patterns. We further show that a structured rotary embedding operator matched to the Kronecker representation preserves the relative-position property of RoPE while rotating only the compact factors, removing the need for a decoupled RoPE branch as in MLA. Empirically, KPA matches or exceeds TPA, MHA, MQA, GQA, and MLA across four model scales and nine downstream benchmarks under identical training conditions, while achieving up to 10x KV cache compression. The Kronecker head split is a tuneable hyperparameter that allows practitioners to navigate the compression-accuracy trade-off at design time without architectural changes.
papers.title_ja: クロネッカー積アテンション：構造化分解によるメモリ効率の良いKV圧縮
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、自己回帰生成におけるKVキャッシュのメモリ負荷を軽減する新しいアテンション機構「Kronecker Product Attention (KPA)」を提案する。KPAはキーとバリューをコンパクトな行列因子のクロネッカー積の和として表現し、既存のTPAを厳密に一般化しながら、より豊かなブロック構造パターンを表現可能にする。さらに、この表現に適合した構造化回転埋め込み演算子により、RoPEの相対位置特性を維持しつつ追加の位置エンコーディング機構を不要にする。実験では、4つのモデル規模と9つの下流ベンチマークにおいて、MHAやGQA、MLAなどの既存手法と同等以上の性能を維持しつつ、最大10倍のKVキャッシュ圧縮を実現した。

papers.title: Mesh-Native Tokenisation: Retrofitting Foundation Models to Unstructured Data
papers.summary: Physics foundation models are an increasingly popular approach for building versatile emulators for spatiotemporal systems. They require tokenisation layers that lift physical field data into a latent representation suitable for dynamic processing. A typical choice for this layer is a convolutional encoder, which lifts field information in a locality-aware way and can be trained very efficiently. However, this choice cannot be applied to a large class of scientific computing problems where data are represented on unstructured meshes, for example simulations on domains with curved boundaries. Such data typically require graph neural network architectures, which are more expensive to train and, in the form currently used, encode information differently from their CNN counterparts, thus limiting the portability of physics emulators between these data regimes. In this work we introduce Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC), a locality-aware tokenisation layer that encodes unstructured mesh-based data in a way that is analogous to CNNs. This approach leads to models that can be trained once on mesh data and then deployed to arbitrary unstructured meshes, even if these are irregular, with minimal retraining. We show that this tokenisation approach can be used to retrofit grid-pretrained foundation models efficiently on unstructured meshes and provide theoretical results to confirm the consistency of this approach with classical CNN encoders. We demonstrate the favourable performance of this retrofitting approach, which in many cases reaches acceptable accuracy even in zero-shot deployment, and outperforms existing baselines after only a few epochs of fine-tuning, thus providing an efficient bridge between the two data regimes.
papers.title_ja: メッシュネイティブトークナイゼーション：非構造化データへの基盤モデルの適用
papers.summary_ja: 非構造化メッシュ上の物理シミュレーションデータに対し、CNNと同様の局所性を持つトークナイゼーション層「Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC)」を提案する。これにより、グリッドデータで事前学習した物理基盤モデルを、再学習の最小化を伴いながら非構造化メッシュへ効率的に転用（リトロフィッティング）できる。理論的整合性を示すとともに、ゼロショット展開でも許容できる精度を達成し、既存ベースラインを上回る性能を実証した。

papers.title: Neural Surrogate Modeling of Ultrasonic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media
papers.summary: Neural surrogates provide computationally efficient auto-regressive modeling of wave propagation, enabling e.g. fast inverse solutions. Despite recent progress, the current surrogates are not yet sufficient for the needs of ultrasonic sensing, characterized by high frequency and heterogeneous propagation media. We show how methods building on Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) fail to capture essential signal features, such as reflections, whereas U-Net -based methods learn the wave fields well but lack the ability to transfer information across different spatial scales. We then propose a new surrogate that captures the best of the two worlds, by integrating FNOs and local-integral resampling into a U-Net architecture. We show it can be trained on limited data, and that the predictions are robust to input noise and work across spatial scales.
papers.title_ja: 非均質媒体における超音波伝播のニューラルサロゲートモデリング
papers.summary_ja: 非均質媒体における超音波伝播を高速にシミュレートするニューラルサロゲートモデルを提案する。既存のFourier Neural Operators (FNO) は反射などの信号特徴を捉えられず、U-Net は空間スケール間の情報伝達に課題があることを指摘する。そこで、FNOとローカル積分リサンプリングをU-Netアーキテクチャに統合した新手法を設計した。限られたデータで学習可能であり、入力ノイズに対して頑健で、異なる空間スケールでも予測精度が維持されることを示した。

papers.title: Hierarchical Graph Neural Network for Probabilistic Power Flow with Grid Topology Contingencies
papers.summary: Data-driven surrogates reduce the nonlinear solves required for probabilistic power flow (PPF), but models tied to a fixed bus--branch graph often generalize poorly when outages change electrical coupling. This paper proposes a topology-decomposition-driven hierarchical bidirectional graph neural network (TDD--HBGNN) for PPF under unseen topologies. For each realized topology, the network is decomposed into fundamental topological units (FTUs), dynamically homogeneous voltage clusters (DHVCs), and a core backbone sub-grid (CBSG), with equivalent-admittance representations preserving electrical ports between units. A sensitivity-based linear prior captures the first-order voltage-magnitude and phase-angle response, while the HBGNN learns topology-dependent nonlinear residuals. Impedance- and uncertainty-aware bottom-up aggregation condenses local perturbations, while mode-modulated top-down broadcasting restores system context at buses. We evaluate our approach on the IEEE 118-bus and Polish 2746-bus systems under unseen N--1 and N--2 contingencies against six baseline methods. Compared with these methods, TDD--HBGNN achieves 2.47--4.20-fold lower all-bus phase-angle errors and lower phase-angle errors in every held-out event. Its voltage-magnitude advantage is concentrated near the outaged branches, where paired error ratios reach 1.75--2.58 on the IEEE system and 1.87--1.97 in Polish N--2 events. All system--contingency--baseline comparisons favor TDD--HBGNN in joint voltage--angle error. Moreover, shared hierarchical operators keep the model size at 0.658 million parameters across both grids and yield 0.161--1.793~ms forward latency per probabilistic case. These results demonstrate system-wide angular accuracy, outage-local voltage accuracy, and parameter-efficient scaling across unseen topologies.
papers.title_ja: 系統トポロジーの障害を考慮した確率潮流計算のための階層型グラフニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 電力系統の確率潮流計算において、系統トポロジーの変化（N-1/N-2障害など）に頑健なサロゲートモデルを提案する。グラフニューラルネットワークを階層構造に分解し、線形な感度ベースの事前知識と非線形な残差学習を組み合わせることで、未知の系統構成でも高精度な電圧・位相角を推定する。IEEE 118バスやポーランド2746バス系統で、既存手法比2.5〜4.2倍の位相角誤差低減と、0.16〜1.8msの高速推論を実現した。パラメータ数は約66万と効率的であり、大規模系統へのスケーラビリティも示している。

papers.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
papers.summary: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.
papers.title_ja: 制約付き確率数値計算：線形不等式制約下における線形偏微分方程式のガウス過程ソルバ
papers.summary_ja: 線形偏微分方程式（PDE）を解くガウス過程ソルバにおいて、等式条件だけでなく不等式制約（非負性・単調性など）を同時に条件付け可能にする手法を提案する。ガウス過程事前分布を線形等式観測と有限次元の不等式事象に順次条件付けする等価性を証明し、非ガウスだが計算可能な後験分布を構築した。ポアソン方程式、オプション価格、大気質データでの評価により、境界データ不完全時やスパースデータ下で、制約の導入により再構成誤差やアービトラージ発生率が大幅に低減することを示した。

papers.title: Electron-Density-Informed Molecular Property Prediction Using Surrogate Functionals
papers.summary: Machine learning methods are increasingly used to predict chemical properties directly from the molecular structure to bypass the often prohibitive cost of quantum mechanical calculations. Recent work has shown that including the ground-state electron density as input to the machine learning model can improve accuracy in this setting. This work employs the recent surrogate functional framework originally developed for orbital-free density functional theory and extends it to predicting molecular properties. We show that passing the ground-state density as input to the model, while simultaneously enforcing it to be the minimum of the surrogate functional, surpasses state-of-the-art performance for six out of seven extensive properties of the QM9 dataset. Additionally, the approach shows improved generalization to larger molecules taken from the QM40 dataset. On all extensive properties of both datasets, our approach outperforms models that are informed by the ground-state density but do not enforce the surrogate functional constraints.
papers.title_ja: サロゲート汎関数を用いた電子密度情報に基づく分子物性予測
papers.summary_ja: 量子化学計算のコストを回避するため、分子構造から化学物性を予測する機械学習手法を提案する。従来の電子密度入力に加え、サロゲート汎関数の最小化制約をモデルに課すことで、QM9データセットの広範な物性において最先端性能を上回る精度を実現した。さらに、QM40データセットにおける大きな分子への汎化性能も向上しており、制約付きアプローチの有効性を示している。

papers.title: Kairos: Toward a Byte-Level Foundation Model for Every Modality
papers.summary: Small language models trained on a single local machine leave little room for architectural trial and error. Kairos combines bidirectional gated-DeltaNet linear attention and sliding-window attention over shared projections (LiZAttention2), block-wise Attention-Residual aggregation, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feed-forward layer and a multi-scale byte-level codec, trained with a uniform-noise denoising objective over one byte space shared by text, image, audio, video, lidar and control streams; this report asks whether the combination optimizes at all before asking whether it is useful. We give code-derived algorithms for each component, including a cross-session recurrent-state memory gate, then run convergence sanity checks: overfittinga single 440-byte sentence at 1--15M parameters, text only, with three seeds for codec and attention choices and single-run sweeps for seven further factors. The two attention variants tested at 3\,000 steps (LiZAttention2 and window attention alone) reach a minimum loss near $10^{-3}$. After 600 steps, the mean minimum loss ranges from 0.018 (patch codec) to 0.354 (depthwise convolutional codec) with an identical ranking on three seeds. An apparent advantage of shared over separate attention projections closes with more steps or more diverse data and reverses when the projections are frozen: it is a convergence-speed effect, not a capacity effect. These checks suggest that the implementation optimizes; they say nothing about generalization, multimodal training or comparison with existing models, which a planned pretraining run is meant to address. The Discussion sizes a 200M-total/25M-active target analytically; none of its throughput figures is measured. Code is available at https://github.com/fabienfrfr/Kairos . Python package at https://pypi.org/project/kairos-fm/ .
papers.title_ja: Kairos: 全モダリティ向けのバイトレベル基盤モデルへ

papers.title: AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits
papers.summary: Autoregressive decoding is less suited to non-causally ordered data, e.g., cross-references or future dependencies, since their outputs cannot be revised post hoc, unlike iterative human reasoning. Diffusion LLMs partially mitigate this limitation but still cannot flexibly insert or remove arbitrary numbers of tokens from a pre-generated context. We design AutoIndexer as a generative model with a novel training and decoding mechanism that simulates a Chain of Edits, allowing the model to flexibly modify its prior outputs in hindsight via token insertions, substitutions, and deletions. The model learns to predict marker tokens for opening and closing edits, simultaneously moving a cursor to positions in the existing token sequence, analogous to a text editor. Training sequences are obtained by perturbing ground-truth labels with inverse chained edit operations, and the model learns to edit by undoing those inverses. The perturbation training allows AutoIndexer to be robust to erroneous context and adaptable to editing tasks such as code correction. We demonstrate that our method exhibits post-generation context-editing capabilities that most autoregressive and diffusion models lack without compromising performance on standard LLM benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/AutodeskAILab/autoindexer.
papers.title_ja: AutoIndexer: 編集チェーンによる因果モデルの訓練を通じた柔軟な順序デコーディング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、自己回帰型LLMの非因果的データ処理における制約を克服するため、トークンの挿入・置換・削除を柔軟に行える「編集チェーン（Chain of Edits）」機構を提案する。モデルはテキストエディタのようにカーソルを移動し、生成済み出力を事後に修正する能力を学習する。訓練では正解ラベルに逆編集操作を適用してノイズを加え、モデルがその逆操作を通じて編集を学ぶことで、誤ったコンテキストへの頑健性とコード修正などの適応性を高める。標準的なLLMベンチマークでの性能を維持しつつ、既存の自己回帰型や拡散型モデルに欠如する生成後のコンテキスト編集能力を実現した。

papers.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
papers.summary: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.
papers.title_ja: SpireBench: Slay the Spireを用いたエージェント型モデルの長期戦略的プレイ評価
papers.summary_ja: 長期的な戦略的推論能力が不足しているエージェント型LLMを評価するため、カードゲーム『Slay the Spire』の完全版をプレイさせるベンチマーク「SpireBench」を提案する。20種のLLMを対象に、フロンティアモデルはヒューリスティックベースラインを上回るが、ゲームの進行に伴い人間のプロゲーマーとの差が拡大する傾向が確認された。特に、リスク評価の誤りや、実行間メモリからの学習不足が性能のボトルネックであることが判明した。本手法は、エージェントの失敗箇所を特定するための包括的な評価ツールとして機能する。

papers.title: Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting
papers.summary: Prompt optimization is an attractive alternative to reinforcement learning for adapting language-model agents, since it is cheap and produces human-readable artifacts. On factual tasks, however, it carries a failure mode that scalar-reward reinforcement learning does not. An optimizer that reads the training examples can write their answers into the prompt, so an in-distribution gain may be memorization rather than transferable behaviour. We apply reflective prompt evolution (GEPA) to the two system prompts of a multi-agent deep-research agent and evaluate it under a topic-disjoint split in which no topic is shared across train, validation, and test. Held-out citation reward rises by 0.079, from 0.702 to 0.781, with a bootstrap 95\% confidence interval of [0.051, 0.107], and the gain replicates across three seeds (mean 0.107). Nearly half of the winning prompt is a memorized answer key, yet a controlled ablation shows this content earns no reward even on the exact training questions it encodes. The large validation-minus-held-out gap is therefore small-sample selection under a noisy judge, not memorization. Varying the verifier isolates what makes the gain transfer. Decomposed per-dimension feedback is the causal ingredient, and collapsing it to a single scalar reward makes held-out transfer negative. The gain persists under an out-of-family judge and is largely reproduced by a hand-written version of the discovered recipe. Credible evaluation of prompt optimizers therefore requires held-out topics, multiple seeds, and verifier ablations. We release the candidate prompts, lineage diffs, figures, tables, and analysis.
papers.title_ja: 深層研究エージェントの反省的プロンプト最適化：トピック非重複・マルチシードプロトコルによる転移可能な利得とプロンプトレベルの過学習の測定
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習の代替手段として、LLMエージェントのプロンプト最適化手法（GEPA）を深層研究エージェントに適用し、トピック非重複な評価プロトコルでその汎化性能を検証した。検証セットとテストセットのトピックを完全に分離することで、プロンプトへの答えの暗記（過学習）と真の転移可能な利得を区別する手法を提案した。結果、分解された次元別フィードバックが利得の転移に因果的に重要であることが示され、スカラー報酬への集約は転移を阻害することが判明した。本手法は、プロンプト最適化の信頼性評価において、保持トピック、複数シード、検証器のアブレーションが不可欠であることを示している。

papers.title: SynAct: Synergistic Active Feedback Learning for LLM Agents
papers.summary: LLM agents executing multi-step workflows fail in two fundamentally different ways: recoverable slips, which further attempts can repair, and knowledge gaps, which retrying cannot resolve. Expert feedback can address the latter, but expert attention is scarce. The key challenge is therefore not whether to ask for feedback, but where feedback can change the outcome. Existing approaches either avoid expert feedback, allowing agents to reinforce their own errors, or allocate feedback at the task level without identifying consequential decisions. We present SynAct, an active learning framework that treats expert attention as the binding constraint and allocates feedback at the level of individual decisions. SynAct ranks decisions by the mutual information between the selected action and the terminal outcome across repeated rollouts, queries an expert at the highest-value decisions, and distills the resulting corrections into transferable rules that the agent can reuse without expert access at deployment. We theoretically characterize what this signal identifies under finite repeated sampling: with k rollouts and at least m observations per action, outcome-constant decisions have zero mutual information, while outcome-separating decisions have mutual information at least H2(m/k) bits, yielding exact separation for any threshold t in (0,H2(m/k)). This also explains why success-based acquisition can be blind when all rollouts fail: success is constant even when failed runs reach different outcomes. Across four agent benchmarks and four models spanning three families, SynAct improves held-out accuracy in all 16 evaluated settings, by +11.7pp on average. The same signal transfers to inference-time routing, where SynAct outperforms budget-matched cascade, uncertainty, and expert-judge routers in 15 of 16 settings, while a single targeted correction outperforms seven additional unaimed retries.
papers.title_ja: SynAct: LLMエージェントのためのシナジスティック・アクティブ・フィードバック学習
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントのマルチステップタスクにおける失敗を「回復可能なミス」と「知識ギャップ」に分類し、限られた専門家フィードバックを最も成果に影響する意思決定箇所に割り当てるアクティブ学習フレームワークを提案する。反復ロールアウトにおける選択アクションと最終結果間の相互情報量に基づいて重要度ランキングを行い、高価値な決定点でのみ専門家から修正を取得する。得られた修正を転用可能なルールとして蒸留し、デプロイ時に専門家アクセスなしで再利用可能にする。4つのベンチマークと4つのモデルで評価し、平均+11.7ppの精度向上と、推論時ルーティングにおける既存手法を上回る性能を実証した。

papers.title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
papers.summary: Data-centric scaling of RLVR has focused on collecting or generating verifiable training problems. However, corpus size alone does not determine whether the dataset provides a useful learning signal for a target policy. To guide the synthesis of effective RLVR data, we experimentally characterize dataset effectiveness as a function of its problems, the target policy, and the training rollout budget. Under this characterization, we show that a large open-source math corpus pooled from widely used RLVR datasets falls almost entirely into a zero-advantage trap: for a fixed target policy and rollout budget, roughly 88% of its problems are solved in every rollout or failed in every rollout. Filtering concentrates what remains, but it can only select, discarding the hard problems. Effective synthetic problems should therefore require the reasoning operations and compositions required to solve those hard problems. Yet their difficulty must be calibrated, so that some rollouts succeed, some fail, and at least one correct solution fits within the training budget. Prompting a teacher to vary hard problems directly does not achieve this. Guided by these empirical principles, we introduce MagicBeanStalk, a top-down decomposition and bottom-up recursive data-synthesis algorithm that grows seed problems into families of substantively new, policy- and budget-calibrated training problems while preserving the seeds' reasoning blueprints. Across 8 math benchmarks, continual RLVR on MagicBeanStalk problems improves gpt-oss-120b from 61.2 to 69.8 (+8.6) and DeepSeek v4Flash from 72.4 to 77.9 (+5.4) on a 16K-token budget. Training on the full 78K source corpus improves by only +1.1 and its best filtered real data subset by +5.8. In finance, we synthesize over 14K verifiable problems from only 340 solutions and improve over base by 6.9 and 2.4 points on SecQue and FinanceBench, respectively.
papers.title_ja: MagicBeanStalk: 再帰的データ合成によるRLVRのゼロアドバンテージトラップからの脱却
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習による検証可能推論（RLVR）において、既存コーパスの約88%がターゲットポリシーに対して学習シグナルを与えない「ゼロアドバンテージトラップ」に陥っていることを実証した。この問題を解決するため、シード問題を分解・再帰的に合成し、ポリシーと推論予算に最適化された新規問題群を生成するアルゴリズム「MagicBeanStalk」を提案する。数学ベンチマークでは、既存データセットのフィルタリングや全量学習よりも大幅な性能向上（最大+8.6点）を実現し、金融分野でも少量の解答から高品質な検証可能問題を合成して精度を改善した。

papers.title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
papers.summary: Language model agents increasingly operate over long interaction streams, requiring online adaptation to distribution shifts through continual learning. However, existing agent harnesses typically either evolve their states only through forward information flow or rely on additional replay or validation data for harness optimization. To address this, we propose ReHarness, a recurrent harness framework for agentic continual learning that complements forward read and write with backward revision under a strictly online streaming protocol. We ask what information could have been captured differently in the harness state to better inform the current instance in the stream. Specifically, after each instance, we leverage the resulting trajectory as feedback to revise the reflections retrieved for that instance, thereby propagating feedback backward through the textual harness state. Across three continual learning benchmarks and three language model backbones, ReHarness consistently outperforms strong raw-context baselines, memory- and reflection-based methods, and prompt optimization approaches. Further analysis shows that ReHarness produces source-grounded and meaningful revisions, corrects overgeneralized or outdated experience under distribution shifts, and improves both stability and plasticity during continual learning.
papers.title_ja: エージェント型継続学習のための再帰的ハーネス
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントが長期間の対話ストリームで分布シフトに適応するための継続学習フレームワーク「ReHarness」を提案する。従来の前向きな情報フローのみや、リプレイデータに依存する手法に対し、厳密なオンラインストリーミングプロトコル下で後方修正（backward revision）を行う。各インスタンス後の軌跡をフィードバックとして利用し、テキストベースのハーネス状態内のリフレクションを遡って修正することで、過剰一般化や古い経験の訂正を実現する。3つの継続学習ベンチマークと3つのLLMバックボーンにおいて、既存のメモリ・リフレクション手法やプロンプト最適化手法を上回る性能と安定性を示した。

papers.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
papers.summary: Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) are promising to deliver privacy-preserving, collaborative intelligence. The decentralized training process is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks that corrupt semantic consistency and factual resilience through malicious model updates. This paper presents a new resilience strategy that prevents semantically corrupted knowledge from propagating during federated aggregation. A defense problem is formulated to jointly maximize global accuracy and suppress manipulated model updates, enabling trustworthy knowledge aggregation without accessing private local data. To strengthen the resilience of FedLLMs, we develop a novel Hypergraph Message Passing Graph Autoencoder (HMP-GAE) framework, where low-rank model updates are represented as nodes in a hypergraph and high-order semantic relationships among multiple agents are exploited through iterative message passing. By leveraging historical checkpoints and cross-agent relational reasoning, HMP-GAE identifies and suppresses semantically inconsistent updates while preserving knowledge alignment among agents throughout federated training. HMP-GAE is implemented using Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3.2 as pretrained FedLLM backbones and evaluated on AG News and Yahoo! Answers datasets. Compared to existing defenses, HMP-GAE improves global accuracy by $1.21$\%, reduces final-model classification semantic entropy by $44.08$\%, and lowers perplexity by $13.34$\%. HMP-GAE outperforms the GAE-based defense by improving the accuracy $1.39$\%, reducing the semantic entropy by $54.5$\%, and lowering perplexity by $35.5$\%.
papers.title_ja: ハイパーグラフメッセージパッシングによるビザンチン耐性連合大規模言語モデル
papers.summary_ja: 連合学習（Federated Learning）における大規模言語モデル（LLM）の訓練に対し、悪意ある更新（ビザンチン攻撃）に耐性を持たせる新手法を提案する。低ランクのモデル更新をハイパーグラフのノードとして表現し、エージェント間の高次セマンティック関係を活用したメッセージパッシングにより、意味的に不整合な更新を特定・抑制する。Qwen-2.5やLlama-3.2を用いた評価において、既存手法と比較してグローバル精度の向上、セマンティックエントロピーおよびパープレキシティの大幅な低減を実現した。

papers.title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
papers.summary: Task-oriented conversational agents remain fragile under realistic conditions, especially when users exhibit non-cooperative behavior. Existing function-calling benchmarks underrepresent adversarial conversation trajectories, thereby limiting the training resources available for developing robust agents. We present MADS (Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation), a synthetic data generation pipeline that produces structured, diverse dialogue trajectories. We inject adversarial conversation, producing validated conversation trajectories that capture realistic, unhappy paths. Using MADS, we construct MADS-Bench: a benchmark spanning six domains, 55 personas, and 1095 conversations, with approximately 66% of conversations containing failure-prone conversation scenarios. We evaluate the robustness of the trained models using a two-stage training approach that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).
papers.title_ja: MADS: 堅牢な対話エージェントのためのマルチエージェント対話シミュレーション

papers.title: REDaCT: Collapse-Free Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
papers.summary: Unlearning in large reasoning models (LRMs) requires removing forget-set information from both the reasoning trace and the final answer. Existing approaches achieve this objective at the cost of reasoning collapse, where the model fails to produce a coherent chain-of-thought (CoT) and does not properly terminate its reasoning process. To address this challenge, we propose REDaCT (REgenerate via Detection and Corrective Tuning), an inference-time unlearning framework for LRMs. REDaCT consists of two key components: (1) a binary leak detector that identifies sentences in the reasoning trace that leak forget-set information, and (2) an embedding optimization module that learns a corrective embedding offline, such that when injected at the first detected leak during inference, it guides subsequent reasoning towards sentences that do not leak forget-set information. Experimental results show that REDaCT completely avoids reasoning collapse, substantially improving reasoning preservation compared to state-of-the-art unlearning methods while maintaining perfect answer forgetting and near-perfect CoT forgetting. Our code is available at: https://github.com/jmaccoby/redact.
papers.title_ja: REDaCT: 大規模推論モデルにおける崩壊を伴わないアンラーニング
papers.summary_ja: 大規模推論モデル（LRM）のアンラーニングにおいて、推論トレースと最終回答から情報を除去する際に生じる「推論崩壊」問題を解決するフレームワークを提案する。本手法は、推論トレース内の情報漏洩文を特定するバイナリ検出器と、オフラインで学習した補正埋め込みを推論時に注入するモジュールから構成される。これにより、推論の一貫性を保ちつつ、回答および推論過程からの完全な情報忘却を実現し、既存手法と比較して推論維持性能を大幅に向上させた。

papers.title: Meta-Reflective Evolution Effectively Improves Production AI Systems
papers.summary: Large Language Model (LLM)-guided evolutionary optimization has successfully improved prompts, programs, and even entire AI systems. Most optimization methods select a candidate from the search frontier, then mutate it in one LLM pass based only on its failures. This focus on the frontier can stall on production AI systems, where isolated failures reveal little about complex, hidden interactions. We introduce CoCoEvolve (Cortex Code Evolve), an evolutionary optimizer built around what we call meta-reflection, wherein an agentic mutator (Cortex Code) selectively retrieves evidence from the entire evolutionary history and probes the live system before verifying and proposing mutations. We apply CoCoEvolve to optimize three classes of production AI systems: data agents, LLM-powered data pipelines, and data engineering workflows. On DABStep, CoCoEvolve tops the public leaderboard, reaching 92.8% held-out hard accuracy compared to 78.4% for Meta-Harness and 30.4% for GEPA under matched conditions. Across six LLM data pipeline workloads, it outperforms every evaluated baseline. On data-eng-bench, CoCoEvolve lifts test-set solve rate from 59.1% to 77.4%, past the best baseline of 73.6%. It also has 11 percentage points higher accuracy than GEPA on HotpotQA while remaining competitive with specialized optimizers on established mathematical and systems benchmarks. Matched ablations confirm that each component of CoCoEvolve contributes to these gains, demonstrating the value of meta-reflection for optimizing production AI systems.
papers.title_ja: メタ・リフレクティブ進化による本番AIシステムの効果的な改善
papers.summary_ja: LLMを用いた進化的最適化手法CoCoEvolveを提案し、本番環境のAIシステム（データエージェント、パイプライン、ワークフロー）の性能向上を実現した。従来の手法が現在の候補の失敗のみを参照するのに対し、本手法は「メタ・リフレクション」により進化履歴全体のエビデンスを選択的に取得し、ライブシステムをプローブしてから変異を提案する。DABStepやdata-eng-benchなどのベンチマークにおいて、既存のベースラインを大幅に上回る精度（例: DABStepで92.8%）を達成し、複雑な相互作用を持つ本番システムにおける有効性を示した。

papers.title: VEPA: Verified Evolving Formal Policy for Lifelong LLM Agent Guardrails
papers.summary: LLM agents increasingly operate over sensitive resources, such as private documents and mutable system states, which can create serious safety and security risks. Runtime guardrails should therefore make inspectable, reproducible, and deterministic allow or refuse decisions before potentially irreversible agent actions are executed. However, safety and security requirements are rarely complete before deployment, so guardrails need to keep adapting as new risks emerge. Existing adaptive guardrails learn from deployment experience, but they usually apply safety policies through LLM inference, which can lead to inconsistent decisions and ambiguous policy interpretations. Formal guardrails, on the other hand, enforce policies deterministically, but they usually rely on pre-deployment or task-specific policies and have no mechanism to adapt to newly observed risks. We introduce VEPA, a framework for the verified evolution of formal agent guardrails. VEPA represents the guardrail as a formal policy of executable symbolic rules over typed agent events. During deployment, we use an LLM guided by deployment feedback to propose policy patches that fix newly observed failures while preserving previously correct behavior. Then, a deterministic verifier only accepts policies that are structurally valid and conflict-free. Finally, an evidence-aware authority layer activates a verified rule only when it has enough supporting evidence, so uncertain updates cannot directly affect guardrail decisions. Across ASSEBench-Safety, ASSEBench-Security, and ATBench, VEPA consistently outperforms baselines while expanding the scope of deterministic formal-policy enforcement. These gains also hold under more challenging deployment conditions, including mixed streams, corrupted feedback, and longer horizons.
papers.title_ja: VEPA: 生涯LLMエージェントのガードレールにおける検証済み進化型形式ポリシー
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントの安全性を確保するため、決定論的な形式ポリシーによるガードレールフレームワークVEPAを提案する。LLMがデプロイメント中のフィードバックに基づきポリシーパッチを提案し、決定論的検証器が構造的妥当性と矛盾の無さを確認する。さらに、証拠ベースの権限レイヤーにより、不確実な更新がガードレール判断に直接影響しないよう制御する。ASSEBenchやATBenchなどのベンチマークにおいて、既存手法を上回る性能と、より困難なデプロイ環境下での頑健性を示した。

papers.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
papers.summary: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.
papers.title_ja: COFFEQA: 反実例ガイドによるLLM質問応答のための少ショット蒸留
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル（LLM）の知識蒸留において、教師モデルの判断境界付近の不確実なサンプルが性能低下を招く問題を指摘する。これに対し、教師モデルの回答を変化させる最小限に修正されたコンテキスト（反実例）を用いて、事実と反実例のペアで学生モデルを監督する手法「COFFEQA」を提案する。さらに、反実例の質を評価する新指標「Context Following Difficulty (CFD)」を導入し、蒸留前の検証を行う。T5やQwen2.5を用いた実験により、従来の事実のみを用いた蒸留と比較して、少ショット予算下で質問応答の精度が向上することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの効率化・蒸留手法であり、ユーザーの関心と直接一致

papers.title: Enriched Holomorphic Neural Networks for 2D and 3D Laplace Problems
papers.summary: Boundary-value problems for the Laplace equation develop singular behaviour near corners, edges and junctions that smooth approximators resolve poorly. We combine holomorphic neural networks with singular functions derived from the local geometry and boundary conditions. The representation is harmonic by construction, so no interior residual is needed: the network fits the smooth remainder from boundary data alone, and the enrichment terms capture the singular behaviour. Singular exponents are trainable, so the construction also applies when the local expansion is not known in advance. We extend the approach to three dimensions using independent networks evaluated along complex null directions. The enriched model is the most accurate tested method on every problem. Its margin is several orders of magnitude where the enrichment captures the singularity exactly, and a factor of about 1.7-2.1 over the next-best method on a CdZnTe radiation detector with many singular sites, in both two and three dimensions.
papers.title_ja: 2次元および3次元ラプラス問題のための拡張ホロモルフィックニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: ラプラス方程式の境界値問題において、角や縁付近の特異性を従来の滑らかな近似では捉えにくい問題を解決するため、ホロモルフィックニューラルネットワークと幾何学由来の特異関数を組み合わせる手法を提案する。この表現は構造的に調和関数となるため内部残差が不要であり、境界データのみで滑らかな残差を学習し、特異項が特異性を捕捉する。特異指数を学習可能とすることで既知の展開がなくても適用でき、3次元へも拡張した。CdZnTe放射線検出器など多数の特異点を持つ問題において、既存手法より数桁から約2倍高い精度を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットとサロゲートモデルの応用であり、数値計算の高速化・高精度化に関わる

papers.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tunes diffusion models with black-box rewards, but reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO are limited in efficiency by poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods such as DiffusionNFT are efficient yet unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average (EMA) off-policy training. We show that NFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward--reverse consistency force that joint positive--negative training cancels only partially, and that EMA stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollouts. We introduce DiffusionART (Diffusion Reinforcement with Aggregation-First Reward Tilting), which aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, removing the consistency force by construction, and adds a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration without EMA tuning. It requires no differentiable reward model, remains effective with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise reward models (DiffusionART-Pairwise). Across image and video generation, DiffusionART trains efficiently and stably without per-task tuning. In particular, on HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion quality rewards, DiffusionART reaches the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast with 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively, while achieving 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards.
papers.title_ja: DiffusionART: 拡散モデルの効率的・安定・スケーラブルな強化学習による強化
papers.summary_ja: 拡散モデルのオンライン強化学習において、逆過程手法の非効率性と正過程手法の不安定性を解決する新しい手法DiffusionARTを提案する。報酬を共有方向に集約することで一貫性力を構造的に除去し、EMAチューニング不要の信頼領域マスク付き更新により安定した学習を実現する。画像・動画生成タスクで、既存手法より大幅に少ないGPU時間と高い報酬達成率を示し、効率的かつ安定した訓練を可能にする。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と拡散モデルの効率化・安定化というユーザー関心に直結する手法

papers.title: Beyond Binary Verifiable Rewards: Behavioral Self-Rewarding for SWE Agents
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision for software engineering agents through executable tests, but binary rewards fail to distinguish trajectories with substantially different debugging quality. We investigate whether the current policy can judge its own trajectories and use these judgments to improve task performance without a separately trained reward model. To this end, we introduce Behavioral Self-Rewarding (BSR), a reward-refinement method that reuses the policy to compare observable debugging behavior among trajectories from the same task with the same verifier outcome. BSR aggregates pairwise preferences into task-local scores and converts them into bounded auxiliary rewards, introducing reward contrast while preserving the verifier-defined pass/fail ordering. This provides additional supervision from already-collected trajectories without requiring new environment interactions. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench-Live show consistent improvements across the evaluated Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B configurations, supporting using the policy's own comparative judgments as a complementary learning signal for training software engineering agents.
papers.title_ja: バイナリ検証可能報酬を超えて：SWEエージェントのための行動的自己報酬
papers.summary_ja: ソフトウェアエンジニアリングエージェントの強化学習において、バイナリ報酬ではデバッグ品質の差異を捉えられない問題を解決するため、行動的自己報酬（BSR）手法を提案する。この手法は、別個の報酬モデルを訓練せずに、現在のポリシー自体が同一タスク内の軌道間を比較し、ペアワイズ選好を有界な補助報酬に変換することで報酬のコントラストを導入する。SWE-bench VerifiedおよびSWE-bench-Liveでの実験により、Qwen3モデルにおいて一貫した性能向上が確認され、既存の軌道から追加の学習シグナルを得る有効性が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と強化学習の高度な応用であり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: Data-driven Optimal Sensor Placement for Aerosol Monitoring in the UK
papers.summary: We develop a data-driven sensor-placement framework and apply it to aerosol monitoring in the United Kingdom (UK). A trained convolutional Gaussian neural process is embedded within the DeepSensor optimisation framework. Genetic optimisation with lazy evaluation and caching reduces mean computational time by 60\% (10$\pm$3 versus 25$\pm$7 minutes) while producing sequential placement performance comparable to the greedy solver. Using the CAMS reference field to construct a retrospective oracle benchmark, Joint NLL improves by about 22\% for Joint-MI-driven genetic placement after five locations for aerosol stations are identified. Seasonal and wind-regime analyses show that agreement between model-based criteria and oracle benchmarks varies with meteorological transport conditions. These results show a computationally efficient approach for data-informed expansion of environmental observing systems.

papers.title_ja: 英国におけるエアロゾル監視のためのデータ駆動型最適センサー配置
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、英国のエアロゾル監視におけるセンサー配置最適化フレームワークを提案する。訓練済み畳み込みガウスニューラルプロセスをDeepSensor最適化フレームワークに組み込み、遺伝的アルゴリズムと遅延評価・キャッシュを活用することで計算時間を60%削減した。CAMS参照場を用いた回顧的オラクルベンチマークにより、5箇所の配置でJoint NLLが約22%改善されることを示した。季節や風場によるモデル基準とオラクルベンチマークの一致度の違いも分析し、環境観測システム拡張への計算効率の高いアプローチを実証している。

papers.title: Amortised Inference through One-Step Implicit Sampling
papers.summary: Efficient sampling from Bayesian posterior distributions in high dimensions remains a hard problem, despite advances in theory and algorithms. Multiple steps are usually required to draw unbiased samples, for example, iterations of an MCMC algorithm or integration steps in a diffusion-based amortised sampler. However, scalable one-step amortised inference remains a challenging open problem. In this work, we build upon recent progress in data-driven generative modelling to offer a possible solution for one-step amortised sampling. Our one-step implicit sampler (OSIS) uses short-time MCMC dynamics to define a local target for the evolution of an implicitly modelled distribution. In the asymptotic limit, the modelled distribution is a fixed point of the MCMC kernel and thus samples from the target. We analyse the convergence properties of OSIS and show connections with other generative modelling and sampling algorithms. We study various design choices and show that OSIS performs well compared to multi-step amortised samplers and non-amortised MCMC baselines while being far more efficient at sampling time.
papers.title_ja: 1ステップ暗黙サンプリングによる償却推論
papers.summary_ja: 高次元ベイズ事後分布からの効率的なサンプリングを目的とし、1ステップで無偏サンプルを生成する暗黙サンプリング手法（OSIS）を提案する。短時間MCMCダイナミクスを用いて分布の進化目標を定義し、漸近的にMCMCカーネルの固定点となることを示す。収束性を解析し、マルチステップ償却サンプラーや従来MCMCと比較して、サンプリング時の計算効率を大幅に向上させつつ同等以上の性能を発揮することを検証した。
papers.relevance_reason: ベイズ推論・サンプリング効率化はML手法全般の関心に直結

papers.title: Neuromorphic Satellite Intelligence: A Formal Framework for Event-Driven Architectures, Spike-Based Algorithms, and Quantitative Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs
papers.summary: Satellite onboard computing faces an irreducible tension: mission intelligence requirements grow monotonically while power, mass, and radiation budgets remain fixed. This paper advances the state of the art on three fronts. First, we develop a formal mathematical model of spiking neural computation for satellite workloads, deriving closed-form expressions for energy consumption as a function of network sparsity, firing rate, and synaptic fan-out. Second, we propose three original algorithms -- a Spiking Kalman-Complementary Filter (SKCF) for attitude estimation, a Temporal Contrast Anomaly Detector (TCAD) for spacecraft health monitoring, and a Spike-Based Adaptive Modulation and Coding (SAMC) scheme for cognitive satellite links -- each with pseudocode and analytical complexity bounds. Third, we introduce a quantitative Energy-Accuracy-Latency (EAL) trade-off surface and populate it with numerical estimates derived from published silicon measurements of Loihi and SpiNNaker, enabling direct comparison with FPGA and GPU baselines. A taxonomy of four radiation-aware neuromorphic architecture classes is refined with fault-rate models. Continual on-orbit learning is formalized through a constrained Spike-Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP) rule that provably bounds weight drift. Case studies for a 12U CubeSat Earth observation mission, a GEO communications payload, and an autonomous deep-space probe provide concrete, quantified design points. Our analysis shows that neuromorphic implementations can achieve 8 to 47 times energy reduction over GPU baselines while maintaining inference accuracy within 2.1\% for representative satellite workloads.
papers.title_ja: ニューロモフィック衛星インテリジェンス：イベント駆動型アーキテクチャ、スパイクベースアルゴリズム、および定量的なエネルギー-精度トレードオフのための形式化フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 衛星搭載計算における電力制約と知能要件の矛盾を解決するため、スパイクニューラルネットワークの形式化モデルを構築し、エネルギー消費の閉形式解を導出した。姿勢推定や異常検知など衛星向けに3つのオリジナルアルゴリズムを提案し、LoihiやSpiNNakerのシリコン測定データを用いたエネルギー・精度・遅延のトレードオフ表面を定量化した。放射線耐性を考慮したアーキテクチャ分類と、重みドリフトを抑制するSTDPルールによる軌道上継続学習の形式化も行う。GPUベースラインと比較し、推論精度を2.1%以内で維持しつつ8〜47倍のエネルギー削減が可能であることを示した。
